findings.claim: The test still reads the page at one instant shortly after load, so an animation that is not drawing its wrong value at that instant, or that finish() jumps past, hides a lasting error. finish() is called on every animation of the checklist and tags whose end time is finite, whatever its play state or how far away that end is, and it un-pauses and ends it; endless animations are read at load time only. Reproduced on a git archive of ea630d09 with the private completed work plus one added rule each, full suite: (F) a finite animation paused with animation-play-state that holds .pack-tag-day at another width; (F2) the same holding a scale on both tags; (G) a finite 100000s no-fill animation holding .pack-tag-day at another width; (G2) a scale animation with an iteration count of 100000; (S1) an infinite alternate scale animation on both tags with a 5s delay, which is cl4-sme-001 variant (b) plus a delay; (S2) the same 5s-delayed infinite animation on .pack-tag-day's width; (S3) a 60s infinite alternate animation with only a to keyframe on .pack-tag-day's width; (S4) the same on .pack-tag-overnight's padding. Every one passes all 12 tests, S1 to S4 in each of three runs. The same unmodified pages opened in the pinned Chromium at 1280x1000 draw the tags wrong: F, F2, G and G2 at 300ms and again about 3s later, S1 and S2 at 5.5s and 6.5s, S3 and S4 at 6s (a tag not 200px wide, laid out at another width, scaled, or with padding other than 12px). So the task 11 Outcome (README line 141, 'exactly 200px wide on screen') and README line 17 ('It rejects scaling ... a tag') are false for these pages, and the class cl4-sme-001 reported is narrowed but not closed. Medium, graded like cl4-sme-001: a wrong page passes, but only after a deliberate keyframes rule, and the completed base widths are still required, so the calculation is not skipped.

evidence.section: 4.4.13 Finishing an animation (finish() silently sets the current time to the associated effect end and resolves the start time, also cancelling a pending pause, so a paused or far-from-ended finite animation jumps to its end state)
animation-play-state: paused (the animation is paused and continues to apply to the element with the progress it had made before being paused)

findings.recommendation: Inspect animations instead of sampling them. For each animation from document.getAnimations() whose target is the checklist, a tag or one of their ancestors: finish it only when its playState is 'running', its end time is finite and its remaining time is short (for example a few seconds). For every other one (paused, delayed, long or endless), read effect.getKeyframes() and fail with a plain message (an animation changes the tag's size) when a keyframe sets a property that changes the box's size or drawn size: width, min-width, max-width, inline-size, padding, border width, margin, box-sizing, display, position, float, scale, rotate, zoom, or a transform that is not a pure translation. Add a paused, a delayed endless and a slow endless variant to the solved-run matrix.

findings.claim: A harmless entrance animation now passes or fails depending only on its fill mode, although the settled page is the same. Without a fill it passes: a 2s fade-in with translate on the tags and a 2s fade-in from a smaller scale on .site-aside each pass all 12. With animation-fill-mode both (the common animate.css-style pattern) it fails: after finish() the fill holds the last keyframe, and the unscaled checks (line 193 for each tag, new lines 146-149 for the checklist) compare the computed strings with 'none' and '1', so an identity value fails. Observed in the pinned Chromium on ea630d09 with the private completed work plus one rule each, full suite: a 0.4s fade-up (opacity plus translateY, fill both) on the tags ending at translateY(0), and the same ending at transform: none, hold transform as matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0) (interpolation extends none with identity functions), and the same with the translate property holds translate as '0px'; each fails task 11 only with '... not by scaling, rotating, moving or zooming it'. The same fade-up on .site-aside holds matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0), and a fade-in from scale .96 to scale 1 on .site-aside holds scale as '1'; each fails task 11 only with 'The gear checklist itself is scaled, rotated, translated or zoomed'. In all five unmodified pages, read about 3s after load, both tags are laid out and drawn exactly 200px wide. The four fade-ups with a translation (three on the tags, one on the checklist) pass all 12 at a942501c, so this is a loop-5 regression for the tags and new with the checklist check. A related, pre-existing case: a 1s no-fill entrance scale on the .page wrapper fails mid-flight with 'something around it is scaling it', because only the checklist's and tags' own animations are finished. Not counted: a static transform: translateY(0) on the tags fails the same way, which README line 17 ('rejects ... translating') arguably covers. Low, graded like cl3-sme-001: the page is valid and the message misdirects, but nothing in the lab asks for an animation.

evidence.section: 11. Interpolation of Transforms (none is extended with identity transform functions, so an animation ending at none yields an identity function list, not none) and the Terminology entry for identity transform function (translate(0), translateY(0), scale(1), rotate(0), matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0))

4.4.13 Finishing an animation (finish() silently sets the current time to the associated effect end and resolves the start time, also cancelling a pending pause, so a paused or far-from-ended finite animation jumps to its end state)

findings.recommendation: Treat geometric identity as unscaled for both the tags and the checklist: transform is none or new DOMMatrixReadOnly(value).isIdentity; translate is none or every component parses to 0; rotate is none or a zero angle; scale is none or every component is 1; zoom is 1. Settling ancestors' short entrance animations as in cl5-sme-001 also removes the .page case. Add a fill-mode both fade-up on the tags and on the checklist to the valid variants of the solved-run matrix.
